added_models.model: Imatinib-sensitive and -resistant GIST cell lines (GIST882, GIST430, GIST48) treated with 17-AAG

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read. 17-AAG (tanespimycin) is an ansamycin Hsp90 inhibitor outside the member list, so product_in_model false.
efficacy.judgement: Cell lines scored as model_kind ex_vivo (in vitro human tumour cells), as for other cell-line tracks.
efficacy.model: Imatinib-sensitive and -resistant GIST cell lines (GIST882, GIST430, GIST48) treated with 17-AAG
efficacy.note: 17-AAG degraded imatinib-resistant KIT and stopped growth of KIT-dependent GIST cell lines, suggesting Hsp90 inhibition would work in imatinib-resistant GIST.
efficacy.short: GIST cells: KIT degraded, growth stopped
efficacy.quote: The dramatic inactivation of imatinib-resistant KIT oncoproteins suggests that HSP90 inhibition provides a therapeutic solution to the challenge of heterogeneous imatinib resistance mutations in GIST patients.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: FDG-PET metabolic partial response 5/23 (22%) with BIIB021, primary endpoint met
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4023320). Dickson cites Bauer 2006 for KIT degradation by Hsp90 inhibitors; NCT00618319 posted no results. FDG-PET is a surrogate.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Dickson cites Bauer 2006 as the rationale but does not set model and trial side by side. Unlike the draft's non-GIST xenograft track, this model is GIST itself.
efficacy.model: Imatinib-sensitive and -resistant GIST cell lines (GIST882, GIST430, GIST48) treated with 17-AAG
efficacy.note: BIIB021 met its primary endpoint in imatinib- and sunitinib-refractory GIST, as the GIST cell lines predicted for Hsp90 inhibition.
efficacy.short: BIIB021 met PET endpoint in refractory GIST
efficacy.quote: This study met its primary end-point.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ganetespib: 0/27 objective responses, clinical benefit (CR+PR+SD >=16 wk) 18.5%; onalespib+imatinib: 19% disease control at 4 months
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results read (first posted 2016-03-10, 27 participants, primary 18.5%, ORR 0%). No prespecified success bar in the registry record; no peer-reviewed ganetespib GIST paper found. Wagner 2016 abstract only.
efficacy.judgement: One drug's contra beats BIIB021's same on this class track: two later members failed to show the activity the cell lines predicted. Quote defines the primary endpoint; the 18.5% and 0% are registry values.
efficacy.model: Imatinib-sensitive and -resistant GIST cell lines (GIST882, GIST430, GIST48) treated with 17-AAG
efficacy.note: Ganetespib gave no objective responses and 18.5% clinical benefit in refractory GIST; onalespib plus imatinib later showed limited activity.
efficacy.short: Ganetespib: no responses in refractory GIST
efficacy.quote: Clinical benefit is defined as showing a complete response (CR), a partial response (PR) or stable disease (SD) for at least 16 weeks.

patient_trials.quote: The combination of onalespib plus imatinib was well tolerated but exhibited limited antitumour activity as dosed in this TKI-resistant GIST patient population.

added_models.model: Primary GIST cells and cell lines expressing PDGFRA D842V treated with IPI-504

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read. Dickson 2012 cites it (ref 14) for activity in inherently imatinib-resistant GIST; its genotyped patients had KIT exon 9/11 only. Wagner 2016 (abstract only, paywalled) reports one PR in a PDGFRA-mutant patient without naming the mutation.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track: the model picks a genotype. Wagner's single PDGFRA-mutant responder could be D842V but the abstract does not say, so no comparison is scored.
efficacy.model: Primary GIST cells and cell lines expressing PDGFRA D842V treated with IPI-504
efficacy.note: IPI-504 degraded imatinib-resistant PDGFRA D842V in GIST cells, predicting D842V patients respond to Hsp90 inhibition; no member trial reported D842V outcomes.
efficacy.quote: Treatment with dasatinib or the heat shock protein 90 inhibitor IPI-504 may provide a therapeutic alternative for GIST patients whose tumors carry the imatinib-resistant PDGFRA(D842V) mutant isoform.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: NCT01039519 started January 2010; Ying 2012 epub December 2011. Abstract only.
